questions.question: What does this print?
questions.detail:
let x = 75
if x > 50 { print("big") } else if x > 70 { print("bigger") }
questions.why: Swift runs the first branch whose condition is true and skips the rest.

questions.question: Why does Swift's switch on a String need a default case?

answers.text: To catch mistakes in the case values
Because a switch must handle every possible value

questions.why: Switches must be exhaustive. There are endless possible strings, so default covers the rest.

questions.question: What values does for i in 0..<3 give?
questions.why: ..< goes up to, but not including, the end.

questions.question: When does a repeat-while loop check its condition?

answers.text: After each pass, so the body runs at least once

questions.question: What does continue do inside a loop?

answers.text: Restarts the loop from the beginning
Skips the rest of this pass and starts the next

questions.why: break ends the loop; continue moves on to the next pass.
